mean: to be left blank and stunned with surprise

near.diff: 開いた口が塞がらない is being dumbfounded by something outrageous, with disapproval; 目が点になる is just stunned bewilderment, often amused.

near.diff: 見栄を張る is putting on a front to look richer or better off; 背伸びをする is reaching beyond one's age or level, often out of eagerness to grow up.

cue: Your thirteen-year-old daughter insists on wearing heels and reading her father's economics books, though she understands little of them. You smile about it.

ctx.s: 中学生[ちゅうがくせい]の娘[むすめ]は{背伸[せの]びをして}、大人[おとな]っぽい服[ふく]ばかり着[き]たがる。
ctx.en: My daughter is in junior high and, wanting to seem grown-up, only wants to wear adult-looking clothes.

ctx.s: 「無理[むり]に{背伸[せの]びしなくて}いいよ。今[いま]の君[きみ]のままで十分[じゅうぶん]だ。」
ctx.en: "You don't have to pretend to be more than you are. You're fine just as you are."

ctx.s: 初[はじ]めてのデートで{背伸[せの]びをして}、飲[の]めもしないブラックコーヒーを注文[ちゅうもん]した。
ctx.en: On our first date I tried to look grown-up and ordered black coffee, which I can't even drink.

ctx.s: 新人[しんじん]なのに{背伸[せの]びをして}、難[むずか]しい仕事[しごと]を一人[ひとり]で引[ひ]き受[う]けてしまった。
ctx.en: I was only a newcomer, but I overreached and took on a difficult job all by myself.

ctx.s: 少[すこ]し{背伸[せの]びをして}、レベルの高[たか]い大学[だいがく]を受験[じゅけん]することにした。
ctx.en: I decided to aim a little high and apply to a top university.

ctx.s: 十代[じゅうだい]の頃[ころ]の日記[にっき]は、{背伸[せの]びした}難[むずか]しい言葉[ことば]ばかりで恥[は]ずかしい。
ctx.en: My teenage diary is embarrassing, full of big words I used to sound grown-up.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は毎日[まいにち]牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]を飲[の]んで、{背伸[せの]びをした}。
bad.en: (meant: he drank milk every day and grew taller)
bad.why: Growing taller is se ga nobiru. Senobi o suru is stretching up on tiptoe, or trying to seem more than one is.

bad.s: 五十代[ごじゅうだい]の父[ちち]が{背伸[せの]びをして}、若者[わかもの]の流行語[りゅうこうご]を使[つか]っている。
bad.en: (meant: my fifty-something father is trying to act young with teen slang)
bad.why: Senobi reaches upward, to seem older or more advanced. Trying to look younger is wakazukuri.
